shortDescription: International Paper NYSE:IP said on Monday its board had approved the spinoff of its Europe, Middle East and Africa packaging business into a standalone publicly traded company, DS Smith, with the separation expected to close on December 7.

children: said on Monday its board had approved the spinoff of its Europe, Middle East and Africa packaging business into a standalone publicly traded company, DS Smith, with the separation expected to close on December 7.
The move advances the packaging maker's plan to create a European-focused packaging business, with International Paper retaining a 19.9% stake in DS Smith
The new business will trade on the London Stock Exchange and New York Stock Exchange under the ticker "SMDS"
International Paper also plans to delist its shares from the London Stock Exchange following completion of the transaction

The company had announced in January that it planned to split into two publicly traded companies by spinning off its EMEA business and that the spun-off unit was expected to be listed in London and New York
The company said in October it was in talks with potential bidders for its EMEA packaging business after unsolicited approaches, opening up an alternative to its planned spinoff of the unit
Shares of the company were up about 2% in premarket trading
